boardMaterials.name: Polypropylene (PP) Commercial Plastic Board
boardMaterials.chemicalLeachingRisk: Low (BPA-free, but sheds polymer chain oligomers and additives)
boardMaterials.description: The most widely used plastic cutting board in commercial and home kitchens. Repeated knife strikes notch and shear semi-crystalline polymer chains, generating thousands of microscopic plastic fibrils that transfer directly into chopped ingredients.

boardMaterials.name: High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Heavy-Duty Board
boardMaterials.chemicalLeachingRisk: Low (phthalate-free, but releases micro-flakes and polyethylene wax)
boardMaterials.description: Standard thick commercial kitchen cutting slab. Softer than polypropylene, HDPE exhibits ductile gouging where knife edges carve curled ribbons and micro-flakes that shear off into moist food.

boardMaterials.name: Low-Density Flexible Plastic Chopping Sheet (LDPE)
boardMaterials.chemicalLeachingRisk: Moderate (plasticizer migration under warm wash cycles)
boardMaterials.description: Ultra-thin, bendable plastic prep sheets. The extremely low polymer modulus allows knife blades to slice deeply into the matrix on the very first prep session, shedding macroscopic shavings and maximum microplastic particle counts.

boardMaterials.name: End-Grain Hard Sugar Maple (Acer saccharum)
boardMaterials.description: The gold standard culinary prep surface. Vertical wood fibers part under the knife edge and spring back together ('self-healing'). Natural capillary action draws moisture down into xylem vessels, depriving bacteria of free water and causing 99.9% osmotic bacterial lysis within 10–30 minutes.

boardMaterials.name: Edge-Grain Laminated Bamboo Board
boardMaterials.polymerClass: Lignified Grass Fiber + Synthetic Resin Binder
boardMaterials.knifeDullingRate: High (natural silica micro-crystals dull blades quickly)
boardMaterials.chemicalLeachingRisk: Low-Moderate (urea-formaldehyde or melamine adhesives in budget boards)
boardMaterials.description: Fast-growing sustainable grass alternative. Highly moisture-resistant and naturally antimicrobial, but high silica content dulls steel knife edges rapidly. Budget boards bonded with cheap adhesives risk glue seam delamination.

boardMaterials.name: Non-Porous Wood Fiber Composite (Richlite / Epicurean)
boardMaterials.polymerClass: Cellulose Fiber + Cured Thermoset Phenolic Resin
boardMaterials.description: High-pressure compressed paper/wood pulp saturated with thermosetting resin. Completely non-porous, commercial dishwasher safe, and highly resistant to deep knife gouges, combining plastic cleanability with wood durability.

boardMaterials.name: Tempered Architectural Glass / Polished Marble
boardMaterials.knifeDullingRate: Catastrophic (destroys steel edge apex in 15–20 strikes)
boardMaterials.description: Zero microplastic shedding and zero bacterial absorption. However, the diamond-like hard surface instantly rolls, micro-chips, and destroys precision knife edges, while lack of blade friction creates severe knife slippage and laceration hazards.

knifeSteels.name: German High-Carbon Stainless Steel (X50CrMoV15)
knifeSteels.description: Standard Western chef knife alloy (Wüsthof, Zwilling). Durable and resilient edge that pushes into plastic without extreme micro-chipping, producing standard sheared polymer fibrils.

knifeSteels.name: Japanese Hardened Powder/Carbon Steel (VG-10 / SG2)
knifeSteels.description: Ultra-hard, laser-thin acute edge. Slices through soft polymers with razor precision, cutting deep narrow micro-crevices (150–400 µm) that trap bacteria deep beyond dishwasher water reach.

knifeSteels.name: Budget Stamped Stainless Steel (420J2 / Rolled Steel)
knifeSteels.description: Soft budget steel that dulls rapidly. The rolled, burred apex tears and plows through plastic rather than slicing, producing ragged microplastic shavings and jagged plastic burrs.

knifeSteels.name: Serrated Utility / Bread Knife (Scalloped Teeth)
knifeSteels.description: The absolute worst knife for plastic cutting boards. The pointed scalloped teeth act as microscopic saws, gouging deep trenches, shredding plastic fibers, and multiplying microplastic particle shedding by 300–400%.

cuttingTechniques.name: Up-and-Down Impact Chopping / Cleaving
cuttingTechniques.description: High downward kinetic impact common when chopping carrots, dense squashes, or portioning poultry. Creates localized impact micro-cracks that flake into food.

cuttingTechniques.name: Center-Pivot Rocking Chop (Herbs, Onions)
cuttingTechniques.description: Knife tip remains anchored while belly rolls over food. Causes high-friction continuous abrasive wear on the exact center of the board, forming a discolored concave depression.

cuttingTechniques.name: Gentle Push/Pull Draw Slicing (Meat, Fish)
cuttingTechniques.description: Low downward pressure drawing the blade horizontally through muscle tissue. Produces clean, minimal plastic displacement and lowest particulate shedding.

cuttingTechniques.name: Rapid Two-Handed Mincing (Garlic, Herbs)
cuttingTechniques.description: Rapid-fire oscillating strikes across a small surface area. Concentrates extreme thermal frictional shear, peeling microscopic polymer fibrils directly into aromatics.

foodTypes.name: Raw Chicken / Turkey Parts
foodTypes.description: Up to 70% of retail poultry carries Campylobacter or Salmonella. Cutting releases pathogen-laden fluid that capillaries down into plastic knife furrows within seconds.

foodTypes.name: Raw Beef, Pork & Ground Meat
foodTypes.primaryPathogen: STEC E. coli O157:H7 & Yersinia enterocolitica
foodTypes.description: Shiga toxin-producing E. coli requires as few as 10 microscopic cells to cause hemorrhagic colitis and kidney failure (HUS) in children.

foodTypes.name: Raw Seafood & Shellfish (Salmon, Shrimp)
foodTypes.description: Marine psychrotrophic bacteria survive cold temperatures and proliferate rapidly at ambient room temperature inside cutting board micro-crevices.

foodTypes.name: Dense Root Vegetables (Carrots, Potatoes, Beets)
foodTypes.description: Hard plant cell walls combined with microscopic silica grit from soil act as an industrial abrasive, maximizing microplastic particle detachment (Yadav et al. 2023).

foodTypes.name: Ready-to-Eat Salad, Cucumbers & Tomatoes
foodTypes.infectiousDose: N/A (Absorbs whatever was on the board)
foodTypes.description: Eaten raw with no cooking or thermal pasteurization. If prepared on a board previously tainted by raw meat, 100% of transferred pathogens enter the digestive tract intact.

wearLevels.name: Brand New (Unscratched)
wearLevels.description: Smooth virgin surface. Liquid easily wipes away; bacterial adhesion is minimal and manual sponge washing is relatively effective.

wearLevels.name: Lightly Used (1–3 Months)
wearLevels.description: Network of shallow knife tracks across main prep area. Sponge bristles begin skipping over micro-crevices, leaving trace residues behind.

wearLevels.name: Moderately Scarred (3–9 Months)
wearLevels.description: Prominent tactile grooves where fingernails catch. Plastic burrs (frayed micro-whiskers) hold organic matter; manual dish soap washing fails to sanitize crevices.

wearLevels.name: Heavily Gouged & Discolored (>1 Year - RETIRE)
wearLevels.description: Deep canyons with gray/black embedded staining. Biofilms have formed an impenetrable Extracellular Polymeric Substance (EPS) barrier. The board cannot be sanitized by any domestic method and must be immediately replaced.

sanitizationMethods.name: Hand Sponge Wash with Cold/Warm Water & Dish Soap
sanitizationMethods.biofilmDisruption: Minimal (Sponge bristles measure ~250 µm; cannot enter 50–100 µm grooves)
sanitizationMethods.spongeCrossContaminationRisk: Extreme (Turns kitchen sponge into Salmonella reservoir)
sanitizationMethods.description: Standard casual rinse. Only cleans surface grease. Bacteria embedded inside knife grooves survive completely untouched, and the sponge transfers pathogens to drinking glasses.

sanitizationMethods.name: Scrub Brush with Hot Water (>55°C) & Heavy Degreaser
sanitizationMethods.biofilmDisruption: Moderate (Nylon bristle tips penetrate wider furrows)
sanitizationMethods.description: Much better than a sponge. Stiff nylon brush bristles dig into furrow openings, disrupting surface organic matter, though deep anaerobic crevice pockets remain viable.

sanitizationMethods.name: Domestic Dishwasher High-Temp Sanitize Cycle (65°C / 150°F)
sanitizationMethods.biofilmDisruption: High (Sustained thermal dwell kills vegetative bacteria)
sanitizationMethods.plasticWarpingDegradation: Severe (Thermal expansion warps boards, opens micro-fissures, accelerates future shedding)
sanitizationMethods.description: Excellent thermal pathogen destruction. However, repeated heat cycles warp thin boards and thermally stress polymer chains, causing plastic boards to shed significantly more microplastics on subsequent cuts.

sanitizationMethods.name: Chlorine Bleach Immersion (200 ppm Sodium Hypochlorite, 2 min)
sanitizationMethods.description: The commercial restaurant health department gold standard (1 tablespoon unscented household bleach per gallon of water). Hypochlorite ions penetrate micro-crevices and oxidize bacterial enzymes.

sanitizationMethods.name: Two-Step Sequential Spray: 3% Hydrogen Peroxide + 5% White Vinegar
sanitizationMethods.biofilmDisruption: High (Forms in-situ peracetic acid on board surface)
sanitizationMethods.description: Scientifically proven non-toxic disinfection protocol (Virginia Tech research). Spraying hydrogen peroxide followed immediately by vinegar forms peracetic acid, destroying Salmonella and E. coli without toxic fumes.

sanitizationMethods.name: Wood Protocol: Warm Water Scrape + Food-Grade Mineral Oil / Beeswax
sanitizationMethods.description: End-grain and edge-grain hardwood maintenance. Mineral oil penetrates xylem tubes, blocking water entry while allowing natural wood tannins and polyphenols to rapidly kill bacteria through desiccation.

presets.name: The Cross-Contamination Trap: Worn Polypropylene + Raw Chicken to Salad
The Microplastic Factory: Daily Carrot Prep on HDPE with Serrated Blade
Executive Chef Gold Standard: End-Grain Maple + Forged German Blade
Budget Plastic Mat Disaster: Flexible Sheet + Dull Stamped Knife

yadavAcs2023.study: Cutting Boards: An Overlooked Source of Microplastics in Human Food (ACS ES&T 2023)
yadavAcs2023.keyFinding: Chopping dense food (carrots) on polypropylene and polyethylene releases up to 7.9 mg of microplastics per 100 strokes, directly ingested with culinary meals.

cliverUcDavis1994.study: Cutting Boards in Salmonella and E. coli Food Safety (Ak & Cliver, UC Davis / USDA)
cliverUcDavis1994.plasticBacterialRecovery: >99% of inoculated bacteria survived inside scarred plastic grooves after hot detergent washing
cliverUcDavis1994.woodBacterialRecovery: 99.9% of inoculated bacteria died within 3 to 10 minutes on hardwood boards without sanitizers
cliverUcDavis1994.mechanism: Wood xylem capillary action draws fluid into deep cells; rapid surface desiccation starves bacteria of required water activity (aw < 0.91).
